assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength lattice proposal and on Ye's demonstrations of ultra-stable strontium clocks, brought fractional uncertainty to the 1e-18 level. This is a clear, original instrument-level advance in precision atomic physics. It has opened tests of fundamental constants, searches for new physics, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second.
assessment.attribution: The two-person configuration is clean: Katori for the lattice-clock concept and early realisation, Ye for the record-setting accuracy, stability and many-body and dense-lattice extensions. Other groups contributed (for example the NIST and PTB groups and Ye's JILA collaborators), but the supplied credit supports a fair two-laureate prize.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across many laboratories with Sr, Yb and Hg clocks is extensive and the clock comparisons are reproducible. Recognition is timely. The 2005 prize covered combs and the 2012 prize covered ion control, so this is a distinct step.
uncertainties: Whether the second will have been redefined by optical clocks is still pending, though that is not needed for the discovery to merit recognition.
Relative weight of the Katori proposal versus the Ye experiments, and the roles of other clock groups, are open to debate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators, together with the later quantum anomalous Hall effect, form a coherent, conceptually deep discovery. It combines a new topological classification of band insulators, protected edge and surface states, and experimental realisation. It has reshaped condensed matter physics and is a natural successor to the 2016 prize on topological phases.
assessment.attribution: Kane (theory of Z2 topological insulators with Mele), Molenkamp (first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe) and Xue (quantum anomalous Hall effect) cover the arc from theory to experiment. Mele, Bernevig, Zhang, Hughes and Hasan are material contributors outside this exact string set, so some credit is left unallocated, and the three-name set mixes two related but different effects.
assessment.maturity: Experiments in HgTe, Bi-based compounds and magnetic topological insulators have been independently reproduced for over fifteen years. The field is mature, though dissipationless-transport applications remain limited.
uncertainties: Credit among the theory pioneers (Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Zhang) and the experimental groups is contested.
Whether quantum anomalous Hall should be recognised together with spin Hall or separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created strong coupling between superconducting artificial atoms and microwave photons, supplying the architecture for dispersive readout and the transmon-based quantum processors. It is original, conceptually clean and has extraordinary downstream impact on quantum technology and quantum optics on a chip.
assessment.attribution: Blais (theory), Wallraff (first strong-coupling experiment) and Schoelkopf (Yale cQED programme, transmon, readout) form a reasonable trio, though Yale colleagues such as Devoret and Girvin and the Cooper-pair-box groups also contributed. The 2025 prize recognised related circuit quantum tunnelling, which may leave cQED credit partly adjacent.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups and now a platform for commercial devices. Timing is good given the 2025 award.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 laureates (Clarke, Devoret, Martinis) and the boundary between cQED and superconducting-qubit credit.
Whether the prize should focus on the physics of coupling or the quantum computing platform.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene linked a precise theoretical prediction of flat bands at a specific twist angle to the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. It opened the new field of moire quantum materials and twistronics, and is original and widely influential.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experiments (with Cao et al.). The set supports a prize with theory and experiment, although the early student and postdoc contributions and other theoretical work (for example Santos, Lopes dos Santos and Peres) raise attribution questions.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many laboratories since 2018, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still being debated. This is a fast-growing field and may be a little early for definitive recognition.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and the microscopic nature of the correlated phases remain unsettled.
Attribution of the theory prediction across several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental implementation made a scalable quantum information processor with atoms concrete. It is an original synthesis of atomic physics and quantum information and is directly tied to the precision control of single ions I know well from my own field.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller proposed the gate; Blatt's group demonstrated the gate and scaled ion processing. Other experimentalists, notably Wineland (already awarded in 2012) and Monroe, are not in the credited set, and gate-scheme alternatives (Molmer-Sorensen) are separate contributions.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups and now a commercial platform. The 2012 prize recognised ion manipulation, which weakens the novelty slightly.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Wineland and Haroche prize and with the duplicate atomic quantum-information candidate (B008) and quantum simulation candidate (B047).
Which part of the proposal-versus-experiment credit is decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave an exact framework in infinite dimensions and a practical method for strongly correlated electrons, including the Mott transition. It underpins modern computational materials theory (DFT+DMFT) and has lasting methodological significance.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar (the mapping to the Anderson impurity model), Vollhardt (with Metzner, infinite-dimension limit). Metzner and Vollhardt's 1989 work and Muller-Hartmann are an important part of the origin, so the supplied three names leave out a decisive contributor.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely used with abundant independent validation, but its predictive success for specific materials is mixed.
uncertainties: Missing credit for Metzner and Muller-Hartmann.
Whether a methodological advance fits the prize as strongly as a physical discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84 and the entanglement-based E91 protocol) established information-theoretically secure communication from quantum mechanics. It is a conceptually original application of quantum foundations and has led to global quantum networks.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced BB84 and Ekert introduced the entanglement-based protocol; Pan's group made the satellite and network demonstrations, but I keep the three originators for a clear configuration. Wiesner's early conjugate coding is a significant historical omission.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are mature and experimental links have been demonstrated repeatedly, though deployment and security of practical systems are still debated. The 2022 prize partly covered related entanglement work.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize (Aspect, Clauser, Zeilinger) and credit for Wiesner.
Practical security issues and uptake are still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP produced precise full-sky maps of the cosmic microwave background and determined cosmological parameters to percent accuracy, establishing the concordance Lambda-CDM model. It is clear, important and had lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page led the instrument and Spergel led much of the cosmological analysis, but the achievement was collaborative and other leaders and the COBE precedent complicate fair credit. Planck later superseded it.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed by Planck and other experiments. Recognition would be late but still plausible; the 2006 and 2019 prizes already covered related cosmology.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration attribution and overlap with earlier cosmology prizes.
Whether the advance is a discovery or a precision measurement of a known framework.
